oneLiner: The only wafer-scale inference platform running in production at scale, sold mostly as a cloud service to a handful of anchor customers. The market is betting that a contracted backlog turns into the promised 2027 revenue step-up, and after Q3 the open question is no longer whether customers want the capacity but whether Cerebras can get the data centers built on time and paid for.

verdict.stance: Neutral - demand passed, delivery did not
verdict.summary: Q3 cleared both numbers we said would turn us Positive (backlog held, Q4 guide far above our bar), and we are still not upgrading. The Q4 step-up is hardware shipments while cloud revenue stalls, the first OpenAI tranches are late for lack of finished buildings, and one quarter of free cash burn consumed a tenth of liquidity. Our base case (2027 core revenue ~2.6x 2026 at 10x EV/Sales) is worth somewhat more than the stock pays, the bear case far less and the bull case far more; that positive skew is thinner than it looks because the model credits today's net cash in full while the build will spend much of it. We turn Positive if the Q4 report shows cloud revenue growing again, a FY2027 framework of at least $2.7B and no terminated OpenAI capacity; Cautious if any OpenAI block is cancelled or liquidity falls faster than $1B a quarter.
wtb: FY2027 core revenue reaches at least ~$2.5B (about 2.6x the $950M FY2026 guide midpoint); the first FY2027 framework is due with the Q4 report (~Feb/Mar 2027).
OpenAI delivery is back on schedule by 2H 2027 with no capacity block terminated, and RPO stays at or above $26B at the Q4 report.
Core gross margin lands in the 47-49% Q4 guide and holds above 45% through 1H 2027 while leased capacity is still in the mix.
The 2027 build is funded from the $7.8B of liquidity plus debt, without a discounted equity raise before end-2027, and the market pays ~10x EV/Sales for a business still growing 50%+ into 2028.

bear.why: Data center delays run through 2027: OpenAI tranches stay late, service credits and a few terminated blocks trim the backlog, and the hyperscaler wins remain small. Core revenue grows ~70% to ~$1.6B, burn forces an equity raise, and the market values a concentrated, capital-hungry hosting-and-hardware vendor.

base.why: Hardware carries 1H 2027 and cloud re-accelerates as owned capacity arrives in 2H; OpenAI is back on schedule late in the year and core revenue reaches ~$2.5B (~2.6x), short of the triple. Core gross margin holds in the mid-to-high 40s and core operating profit turns positive, but GAAP losses and capex persist, holding the multiple near 10x.

bull.why: The triple lands (~$3.0B): buildings arrive on the revised schedule, CS-5 ships from mid-2027, and Microsoft, Oracle and AWS add revenue outside the backlog. Core operating margin reaches the high single digits and fast inference is priced as a category with Cerebras as the non-Nvidia standard.

scenarioModel.note: Revenue is core revenue (GAAP plus customer-warrant amortization, less pass-through data center costs), the basis of company guidance. Value per share = (rev x EV/Sales + current net cash) / current shares, applied to FY2027 core revenue at end-2027. Neither dilution nor capex funding is reflected: the page uses today's share count and today's net cash, while 2027 capex, lease commitments, stock comp and customer warrants will reduce cash and add shares, so every case is overstated, the bear case most. Scenario inputs are Siberforge estimates, not consensus.

debates.q: Does the OpenAI contract convert on time, or leak credits and cancellations?
debates.bull: It is take-or-pay for 750MW with an option on a further 1.25GW; management blames land, power and building shells rather than chips, calls the delay credits already deducted from backlog a worst case, and says OpenAI's own sites are late too.
debates.bear: Initial tranches were behind schedule at Sep 30 and credits began accruing Oct 1; a block 90 days late can be terminated, catch-up is not expected until 2H 2027, and OpenAI has already shown it will run its newest fast mode on Nvidia.
debates.view: The old signpost split: RPO passed (above our $25B bar) but 'capacity on schedule' failed. That moves the debate from whether OpenAI stays to whether Cerebras can deliver, which is a better problem but not a solved one. With under 5% of committed MW terminable in 2026 the floor holds; we treat slippage as a 2027 revenue-timing risk and move to the bear case only on an actual termination.

signpost.metric: RPO, delay credits and any terminated OpenAI capacity block
signpost.threshold: RPO at or above $26B with no block terminated = base holds; a termination or RPO below $25B = bear

debates.q: Is the Q4 step-up the start of the triple, or a hardware pull-forward?
debates.bull: About a third of RPO is scheduled to be recognised in the 24 months to Sep 2028, which by itself roughly supports a triple; hardware now ships at much higher prices and CS-5 production was pulled forward to early summer 2027.
debates.bear: GAAP revenue growth has slowed for three quarters (+94%, +74%, +55% YoY), cloud is guided flat in Q4 because capacity arrives too late, and hardware is the lumpy, lower-margin line that depends on customers' own sites being ready.
debates.view: The old signpost resolved bullish: the Q4 guide beat our $265M bar by ~20%, so the deceleration is supply-gated, not demand-gated. But hardware-led growth earns a lower multiple than cloud, which is why base stays at 10x. The reverse DCF on this page asks for less than the trailing growth rate, yet for seven years, and the trailing rate is flattered by a tiny base that is already slowing.

signpost.metric: Q4 core revenue, Q4 core cloud revenue and the FY2027 revenue framework
signpost.threshold: Q4 at or above $320M with cloud above $145M and a FY2027 framework of $2.7B+ = Positive; Q4 below $310M or a framework below $2.3B = bear

debates.q: Can the balance sheet fund the build without new equity?
debates.bull: Liquidity is $7.8B with $850M of undrawn debt capacity, core operating margin is guided to breakeven in Q4, and owned capacity is already lifting cloud margins.
debates.bear: Q3 free cash flow was -$839M (operating cash flow -$341M, capex $497M); TTM operating cash flow is -$399M, TTM capex is 161% of revenue, and ~$8.5B of leases have not yet commenced. Cash alone ($3.1B, excluding investments) covers two years of TTM burn.
debates.view: We previously called this a valuation issue, not a solvency one; that is now too relaxed. The old margin signpost is on track (core gross margin 41.0%, Q4 guide above our 43% bar), but at the Q3 burn rate total liquidity lasts a little over two years, not five. We assume an equity or convertible raise by 2028 in the bear case and treat a burn above $1B a quarter as the trigger to cut.

signpost.metric: Core gross margin and quarter-end cash, restricted cash and investments
signpost.threshold: core GM at or above 47% and liquidity at or above $7.0B = funded; GM below 45% or liquidity below $6.5B = bear

thesis: Architecturally different, not a GPU clone. Wafer-scale SRAM keeps model weights on-die, which wins on tokens per second for agentic and reasoning workloads, and needs no HBM or CoWoS - the two chokepoints every GPU vendor queues for.
Cloud is the engine and the better business. Core cloud gross margin of 46.9% compares with 31.0% for core hardware, so every owned megawatt that comes online lifts both growth and margin.
Contracted visibility few companies this size have. RPO is about 27x FY2026 guided core revenue, and 700MW of data center capacity is under contract for delivery by end-2027.
Demand is broadening beyond two customers. Microsoft, Oracle (OCI availability in 2027) and AWS have all signed in six months, and none of the three is in the backlog or in revenue yet.

Core economics are turning. The Q4 guide takes core operating margin from -14% to breakeven in one quarter, which is the first evidence the model has operating leverage once capacity is owned rather than leased.

latestProse: Q3 FY2026 (ended Sep 30; reported Nov 12). Core revenue of $230.9M rose 70% and beat the guide by about $16M, with core gross margin a point above the range, and management raised the year. The mix did the work: core cloud and services grew 272% to $144.9M while core hardware fell 11%. GAAP revenue of $210.8M (+55%) sits below core because $36.4M of customer-warrant amortization is booked as contra-revenue; core also strips out $16.4M of pass-through data center costs billed to specific customers. The GAAP operating loss of $224.1M is mostly $155.1M of stock comp. Two disclosures matter more than the beat. First, delivered capacity under the OpenAI agreement was behind schedule at quarter-end; RPO of $26.1B is stated after deducting management's estimate of the resulting service credits. Second, concentration is unchanged in kind: two customers were 38% and 34% of GAAP revenue (OpenAI $72.4M, the other a UAE related-party group identified as MBZUAI in secondary coverage). The stock rose 11% the next session and gave the gain back within a week; the IPO lock-up fully expired on Nov 9.
guidanceProse: Q4 2026: core revenue $310-330M (about +39% QoQ at the midpoint), core gross margin 47-49%, core operating margin -1% to +1%. FY2026 raised to core revenue $940-960M (from $880-890M), core gross margin 42-44% and core operating margin -10% to -8% (from -19% to -17%). No GAAP guidance is given. On the call management said cloud revenue will be roughly flat in Q4 because new capacity arrives too late, hardware moves toward half the mix in Q4 and Q1 2027, the OpenAI schedule is recovered in 2H 2027, and revenue will more than triple in 2027 (no figure given). It also disclosed a cloud inference contract with Microsoft, with details promised in 2027. No new financing was announced.
segments: Cloud and inference services (~63% of Q3 2026 core revenue): tokens and dedicated capacity sold through Cerebras Cloud, the OpenAI agreement and partner marketplaces. Growth is gated by data center deliveries, not demand.

Hardware systems (~37%): CS-3 and CS-4 systems for sovereign, research and now hyperscaler buyers; lumpy, lower margin, and where warrant amortization hits GAAP revenue hardest. CS-5 production is planned for early summer 2027.
Customers: OpenAI and the UAE group (MBZUAI, G42) dominate revenue and OpenAI most of the backlog; AWS, Oracle and Microsoft are signed but pre-revenue. FY2025 revenue was 86% UAE entities.
competitive: Nvidia is the default and bought Groq for $20B in Dec 2025 - a direct fast-inference response, and per SemiAnalysis (Sep 30, 2026) the hardware behind OpenAI's newest Ultrafast mode.
AMD is a partner rather than a rival here: wafer-scale integrated with Helios for disaggregated inference (vendor-claimed up to 5x throughput); Cerebras uses AMD GPUs for prefill in its own cloud.
Hyperscaler ASICs (TPU, Trainium, Maia) and Broadcom/Marvell custom silicon compete for the same inference budgets, even as three hyperscalers sign up to resell Cerebras.
Risk to the speed premium: commodity GPU token prices falling faster than customers will pay for latency.
moat: Wafer-scale SRAM is hard to replicate and demonstrably fast at inference, but the moat is narrow: one TSMC process with no second source, and Nvidia can buy or build fast inference while bundling an unmatched software ecosystem. The backlog is the strongest moat evidence, and Q3 showed its weak point is physical: the chips exist, the buildings to put them in do not yet.
risks: Delivery is now the binding constraint. Land, power and building shells, not chips, set 2027 revenue; more than 75% of 2027 capacity sits outside the US, and every late tranche under the OpenAI agreement costs credits and opens a termination right.

Two customers are most of the business. The top two were 72% of Q3 GAAP revenue and OpenAI is the majority of RPO, so a routing or scheduling decision at one counterparty reprices the stock, as the September SemiAnalysis report showed.

The build may outrun the balance sheet. Free cash burn is accelerating faster than revenue (debate 3), and uncommenced lease commitments exceed total liquidity; a slower ramp means a raise on worse terms.

GAAP losses and dilution are structural. GAAP operating margin has run -20%, -8%, -265% and -106% over the last four reported quarters; ~$1.09B of customer-warrant assets will keep depressing GAAP revenue, and stock comp is annualising above $600M at the Q3 rate.

Reported growth is slowing and getting lumpier. The Q4 step-up rests on hardware shipments that depend on customers' sites being ready; a slip there turns the 2027 triple into a target rather than a plan, and Nvidia-Groq competes for the same budgets in the meantime.
catalysts: Dec 31, 2026: end of the window in which under 5% of OpenAI's committed MW becomes terminable - any cancellation notice is a bear trigger (debate 1).
Late Jan-early Feb 2027: MSFT, AMZN, GOOGL, META Q4 calls - inference capex and any detail on the Microsoft and AWS deployments (debate 2).
~Feb/Mar 2027 (date unverified): Q4 2026 results - Q4 core revenue vs $310-330M, cloud vs hardware mix, FY2027 framework, RPO net of credits, liquidity (debates 1, 2, 3).
~May 2027: Q1 2027 results - first read on 2027 burn and whether cloud revenue is growing again (debates 2, 3).
Early summer 2027: CS-5 enters production; Oracle Cloud Infrastructure availability during 2027 (debate 2).
2H 2027: OpenAI delivery schedule due to be recovered; 700MW of contracted capacity due by end-2027 (debate 1).

valPresets.note: Pre-scale company with four public quarters of history; TTM revenue uses GAAP (below core revenue by warrant amortization). Values the terminal business off a revenue path, horizon FCF margin and exit multiple. The reverse DCF growth rate sits below the trailing track record, but it must be sustained for seven years from a base whose growth is already slowing (debate 2).

changelog.change: Q3 2026 (reported Nov 12): core revenue $230.9M beat the guide, Q4 guided to $310-330M and FY2026 raised to $940-960M, RPO $26.1B. Both numeric conditions we set for an upgrade were met, but the view did not move: stance stays Neutral because the first OpenAI tranches are late on data center construction, the Q4 step-up is hardware while cloud is flat, and Q3 free cash flow was -$839M. Scenarios nudged up on the higher base (bear $1.6B x 6 / base $2.5B x 10 / bull $3.0B x 13); debate 1 reframed from OpenAI loyalty to delivery, debate 3 from capex returns to funding.
